title: A bounded continuous Bobkov integrand
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with $0\le f(x)\le1$ for every $x$, and let $D$ be a continuous map from $\mathbb R^n$ to the space of continuous linear functionals on $\mathbb R^n$. Suppose there is a real number $M$ such that $\|D(x)\|\le M$ for every $x$. Then there is a bounded continuous function $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfying, for every $x$,
\[F(x)=\sqrt{U(f(x))^2+\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(D(x)e_i)^2},\]
where $U$ is the Gaussian profile with zero values outside $(0,1)$ and $e_i$ are the coordinate unit vectors.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,1]$ be continuous, and let $D(z)$ be a continuous family of real linear functionals on $\mathbb R^n$ with $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for all $z$, for some real $M$. Then $z\mapsto\sqrt{\overline I(f(z))^2+\sum_i(D(z)e_i)^2}$ is a bounded continuous function.
